questions.q: Which of the following is NOT an essential assumption for modeling a random variable with a Poisson distribution $\text{Po}(\lambda)$?
choices: Events occur at a variable rate over time
The average rate of occurrence $\lambda$ is constant
Two events cannot occur at the exact same instant
questions.answer: In a Poisson process, events must occur at a constant average rate, independently, at random, and singly.

questions.q: The random variable $X \sim \text{Po}(3.2)$. Find $P(X = 2)$ correct to 4 decimal places.
If $X \sim \text{Po}(\lambda)$ and $P(X = 0) = 0.05$, find the value of $\lambda$.
What is the theoretical relationship between the mean and variance of a Poisson distribution $X \sim \text{Po}(\lambda)$?
questions.answer: A defining property of the Poisson distribution is that its mean and variance are equal: $E(X) = \text{Var}(X) = \lambda$.

questions.q: Independent random variables $X \sim \text{Po}(2)$ and $Y \sim \text{Po}(3)$ represent customer arrivals. What distribution does $X + Y$ follow?
questions.answer: The sum of independent Poisson variables is also Poisson: $X + Y \sim \text{Po}(\lambda_X + \lambda_Y) = \text{Po}(2 + 3) = \text{Po}(5)$.

questions.q: Faults on a fiber optic cable occur at an average rate of 0.4 per kilometer. What is the probability of finding exactly 1 fault in a 5-kilometer section?

sections.heading: Section 3: Poisson Approximation to the Binomial

questions.q: Under which conditions can a binomial distribution $B(n, p)$ be well approximated by a Poisson distribution?
questions.answer: The Poisson approximation to the binomial is appropriate when the number of trials $n$ is large ($n > 50$) and the probability of success $p$ is small ($np < 5$), with parameter $\lambda = np$.

questions.q: A book of 400 pages contains 200 typographical errors distributed at random. Use a Poisson approximation to find the probability that a randomly chosen page contains no errors.
A factory produces screws, of which 1% are defective. In a random sample of 250 screws, what is the Poisson parameter $\lambda$ to model defective screws?

sections.heading: Section 4: Normal Approximation to the Poisson Distribution

questions.q: Under what condition can a Poisson distribution $X \sim \text{Po}(\lambda)$ be approximated by a normal distribution?
questions.answer: When $\lambda > 15$, the distribution is sufficiently symmetric to be approximated by $N(\lambda, \lambda)$.

questions.q: If $X \sim \text{Po}(36)$, which normal distribution provides the best approximation?
questions.answer: Since mean and variance of $\text{Po}(\lambda)$ are both $\lambda$, the approximating normal distribution is $N(\lambda, \lambda) = N(36, 36)$.

questions.q: For $X \sim \text{Po}(36)$, use the normal approximation with continuity correction to state the calculation for $P(X \leq 40)$.
questions.answer: For discrete $X \leq 40$, the continuity correction extends to the upper boundary $40.5$: $P(Y < 40.5)$.
